claims.text: The component material is susceptible to hot cracking during melting because of its physical and microstructural characteristics.
Friction stir repair is a solid-state processing method.
Friction stir repair can restore the damaged component.
Friction stir repair avoids the hot-cracking problems associated with traditional fusion-welding repair.
Friction stir repair uses localized plastic deformation and frictional heating to join or repair material without full melting.
Friction stir processing produces a refined grain structure in the repaired zone.
Friction stir processing minimizes residual stress in the repaired zone.
Refined grains and minimized residual stress mediate improved repair performance.
Friction stir repair keeps localized heating below the material's melting point.
Avoiding a liquid phase reduces the associated hot-cracking risk.
The refined repair microstructure maintains mechanical performance similar to or better than that of the base material.
The friction stir repaired region will resist cracking better under aggressive conditions than a fusion-welded repair.
Friction stir repair will provide a durable, high-integrity repair that enables continued service.
Traditional fusion-welding repair has an inherent hot-cracking risk that causes poor joint quality.
Fusion-welded repairs will eventually fail prematurely under aggressive service conditions.

Friction stir repair is expected to remain effective up to the maximum anticipated service temperatures, pressures, and dynamic loads, provided the material's fatigue and thermal thresholds are not exceeded.
